questions.q: What is created in step 3 of the trail, once an expense item is approved?
options: A cash advance
A corporate card program
The accounting event in Subledger Accounting (debit expense, credit liability)
A new business unit
questions.explain: Once approved, Subledger Accounting generates the accounting event — the debit to an expense account and credit to a liability account.

questions.q: What does Process Expense Reimbursement create in step 4 of the trail?
options: A standard Payables invoice referencing the originating expense report
A new expense policy
A corporate card feed mapping
A journal entry directly in the GL with no invoice
questions.explain: Process Expense Reimbursement generates a standard Payables invoice, carrying a reference back to the original expense report.

questions.q: What does the payment entry generated in step 5 do to the liability created in step 3?
options: It doubles the liability
It has no effect on the liability at all
It creates a brand-new, unrelated liability
It clears the liability, typically debiting the liability account and crediting Cash
questions.explain: The payment accounting entry clears the liability that was created when the original accounting event posted, by debiting the liability and crediting cash.

questions.q: If an expense report shows as approved, but the employee says they were never paid, where should a consultant most likely look first?
options: Back in the original expense item entry screen
The Payables payment process
The expense report template
The audit list rule configuration
questions.explain: Approval happening correctly but payment not occurring points toward an issue in the Payables payment process, since that is the stage that answers 'has this been paid?'

questions.q: Why would a consultant need to trace this entire trail BACKWARD, starting from the General Ledger?
options: Because a CFO noticing an unusually high GL balance (e.g. Travel & Entertainment) needs that number traced back to the specific expense reports and items that drove it
This never happens in practice
Because the General Ledger never contains any expense-related balances
Because backward tracing is illegal under Oracle's terms of use
questions.explain: Consultants often work this trail in reverse, starting from an unexpected GL balance and tracing back through accounting events to the originating expense reports.
